title: Public API GET /executions ignores projectId filter for member API keys
thread_text:
TITLE:
Public API GET /executions ignores projectId filter for member API keys

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
### Bug Description

`GET /api/v1/executions?projectId=<id>` only applies the `projectId` filter when the API key belongs to a user with the global `workflow:read` scope (instance owner/admin). For an API key owned by a regular **member**, the `projectId` query parameter is silently ignored and the endpoint returns executions from **all** projects the member has access to.

Consequences for member API keys:
- `projectId=<project A>` and `projectId=<project B>` return the identical merged result set (all accessible projects mixed together).
- `projectId=<project the member has no access to>` returns the member's full execution list instead of an empty list.
- `projectId=<nonexistent id>` also returns the full list (an owner/admin key correctly returns `[]` in both of these cases).

**Root cause:** in `packages/cli/src/workflows/workflow-sharing.service.ts`, `WorkflowSharingService.getSharedWorkflowIds()` destructures `projectId` from its options, applies it in the `hasGlobalScope(user, 'workflow:read')` branch, but never uses it in the non-global branch — the `where` clause there filters only by workflow role and the user's project relations. Verified identical in `n8n@2.26.3` and current `master`.

Adding the missing condition fixes it (verified locally; existing `workflow-sharing.service.test.ts` and public-api `executions.test.ts` suites still pass):

```ts
const sharedWorkflows = await this.sharedWorkflowRepository.find({
 where: {
 ...(projectId && { projectId }), // <-- was missing
 role: In(workflowRoles),
 project: {
 projectRelations: {
 userId: user.id,
 role: In(projectRoles),
 },
 },
 },
 select: ['workflowId'],
});
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Licensed instance with projects/sharing enabled.
2. Create a **member** user; add them as project admin (or editor/viewer) to a team project that contains a workflow with at least one execution. The member's personal project should also contain a workflow with an execution.
3. Create an API key for the member.
4. Call `GET /api/v1/executions?status=success&projectId=<team project id>` with the member's key.
5. Observe the response contains executions from the member's personal project as well — and that changing `projectId` to any other value (including a nonexistent id) returns the same result set.
6. Repeat with an instance owner's API key: filtering works correctly.

### Expected Behavior

`projectId` should restrict results to the given project for any API key (and return an empty list for projects the key's user cannot access), matching the owner/admin behavior and the documented parameter.

### Debug Info

Reproduced on 2.26.3 (self-hosted) and on current master from source. The relevant code path is unchanged between the two.

### Operating System

Linux (Kubernetes) / also reproduced on macOS from source

### n8n Version

2.26.3 (code identical on master)

### Node.js Version

22.x

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Execution Mode

queue (also reproduced in regular mode)

### Hosting

self hosted

title: Instance-wide Code node runner failures — multiple unrelated workflows affected
thread_text:
TITLE:
Instance-wide Code node runner failures — multiple unrelated workflows affected

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
Instance: pareiprogramei-n8n.cloudfy.live
Since approximately 15:54 (Jul 20), Code nodes across multiple unrelated workflows on this instance have been failing with:
"Task request timed out after 20 seconds — Your Code node task was not matched to a runner within the timeout period. This indicates that the task runner is currently down, or not ready, or at capacity, so it cannot service your task."
This is not isolated to one workflow — it's affecting the entire instance:

PAREI PROGRAMEI | MOTOR PRINCIPAL — Code node executions failing since 15:54 (confirmed via execution history: 15:00/15:26/15:43 succeeded, everything from 15:54 onward failed with the runner timeout error)
PAREI FUTVIRTUAL and FUTVIRTUAL | REGISTRAR JOGOS — separate, unrelated workflows, currently failing repeatedly every few minutes (executions #70139 through #70150 observed, all "Error" with ~20s runtime, running roughly every 8 minutes from 18:53 to 18:59)

All affected Code nodes are simple operations (array mapping, field additions) that normally complete in milliseconds — this is not a code complexity or timeout-tuning issue, it's the task runner itself being unavailable.
Could you please check the runner health/capacity for this instance? This is currently blocking production workflows.

DISCUSSION:
Hey @PareiProgramei,

Thank you for reaching out! We’ve received your issue and are looking into it. To help us track this internally, we’ve created a Linear ticket with the reference: "GHC-9032".

We’ll keep you updated as we make progress, but if you have any additional details or context to share, feel free to add them here - it’s always helpful!

Thanks for your patience and for bringing this to our attention.

---
> For *INTERNAL* use only: [GHC-9032](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/GHC-9032)

--- COMMENT ---

@PareiProgramei this error is the by-design runner timeout. `TaskRequestTimeoutError` fires when no task runner accepts a Code node task within `N8N_RUNNERS_TASK_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (~20s). The instance-wide, timestamped onset across unrelated workflows points to the task runner process being down, unreachable from the main instance, or at capacity on your deployment. It is not a Code node complexity issue.

Your instance runs on `cloudfy.live`, which is a third-party host, not n8n Cloud. We have no access to the runner health or capacity there, so this is best raised with Cloudfy support. On your side, worth checking whether the runner container is up and healthy, and whether it can reach the main instance (auth token and network).

title: Bug: Formula filter "Return Type" allows inconsistent selections
thread_text: TITLE: Bug: Formula filter "Return Type" allows inconsistent selections ISSUE DESCRIPTION: ### Bug Description When configuring a filter for a Formula property in the Notion node, the Return Type dropdown allows selecting any supported type (Text, Number, Checkbox, Date, etc.), even if the selected Formula property evaluates to a different type. This allows users to construct requests that the Notion API immediately rejects with a validation error. ### To Reproduce 1. Create a Notion Formula property that returns a checkbox (boolean), for example: prop("Status") == "Done" 2. In the Notion node: - Resource: Database Page - Operation: Get Many - Filter: Build Manually - Property: Formula property - Return Type: Text - Condition: Is Not Empty 3. Execute the node. ### Expected behavior Formula properties in notion have a specific return type based on the formula expression. Only this return type should be used while calling the notion api using the property. The n8n UI should ideally prevent users from selecting inconsistent return types for Formula properties, or otherwise validate the selection before sending the request. If automatic detection of the Formula return type is possible, the node could restrict the available options (or automatically select the correct one). If automatic detection is not possible due to limitations of the Notion API, it may still be worth improving the UX by documenting the requirement more clearly or validating the configuration where feasible. ### **Actual Behaviour** The ui lists all the possible return types for the formula property. Choosing the wrong one can generate errors like: `{ "object": "error", "status": 400, "code": "validation_error", "message": "The formula has a result type that does not match the property type of the filter provided: formula checkbox does not match filter text", "request_id": "ba1ef1c8-dfe0-42ea-aa62-aaaed8185906" }` _Fixing this is only possible if notion provides a way to expose the return type of its "formula" properties._ _Othewise building a expression parser to get the return type for "formula" properties can work._ **### Question** Does the Notion API expose the evaluated return type of a Formula property through any endpoint (for example, as part of the database/data source schema)? If so, n8n could potentially use that metadata to present only valid return type options for the selected Formula property. ### Debug Info # Debug info ## core - n8nVersion: 2.32.0 - platform: npm - nodeJsVersion: 22.23.1 - nodeEnv: undefined - database: sqlite - executionMode: regular - concurrency: -1 - license: community - consumerId: unknown ## storage - success: all - error: all - progress: false - manual: true - binaryMode: filesystem ## pruning - enabled: true - maxAge: 336 hours - maxCount: 10000 executions ## client - userAgent: mozilla/5.0 (windows nt 10.0; win64; x64) applewebkit/537.36 (khtml, like gecko) chrome/150.0.0.0 safari/537.36 - isTouchDevice: false ## cluster - instanceCount: 1 - versions: 2.32.0 - instances: - instanceKey: f8073990-aa0d-4a31-9f01-943f4582abcc, hostId: main-UGeK0u2YGtoga72y, instanceType: main, instanceRole: leader, version: 2.32.0 - checks: - check: hostid-clash, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: lifecycle, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: split-brain, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: version-mismatch, status: succeeded, warnings: - Generated at: 2026-07-22T08:34:16.371Z ### Operating System Windows ### n8n Version 2.32.0 ### Node.js Version 26.5.0 ### Database PostgreSQL ### Execution mode main (default) ### Hosting n8n cloud DISCUSSION: Hey @tusharmotwani1718, Thank you for reaching out! We’ve received your issue and are looking into it. To help us track this internally, we’ve created a Linear ticket with the reference: "GHC-9050". We’ll keep you updated as we make progress, but if you have any additional details or context to share, feel free to add them here - it’s always helpful! Thanks for your patience and for bringing this to our attention. --- > For *INTERNAL* use only: [GHC-9050](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/GHC-9050) --- COMMENT --- On investigating further down the api, I found that the notion doesn't exposes the return type for formula properties directly while fetching the properties of the data source. Instead to get the return type, we need to call the api for "Query a single page" i.e. `data_sources/${dataSourceId}/query`. Although, using this extra api call has both: **Pros**: - Better UX - Prevents invalid filter combinations - No confusing Notion validation errors **Cons**: - Extra API request while configuring the node - Slower parameter loading This is an important design decision and over to n8n team. also, I can raise PR for this if you guys agree to change the current flow a bit and add an extra api call. --- COMMENT --- This seems to be a duplicate of: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/34590 --- COMMENT --- > This seems to be a duplicate of: [#34590](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/34590) Just checked out the issue #34590 While both the issues seem similar, there is a slight difference between them. #34590 issue is about fetching the pages with unknown formula type. However this issue is about showing fixed return type in n8n ui for already present formula return type to avoid inconsistent parameters. That means the formula already has a return type and it is fixed so the n8n ui should only show that return type instead of giving a fixed list of options everytime. Have also shared my technical investigation over the current working notion node in this issue's comment. --- COMMENT --- @tusharmotwani1718 Good to know, thank you 🙌 --- COMMENT --- Hi! I'd like to work on this issue. I have experience with AI/ML projects and this aligns well with my skills. I'll submit a PR soon! 🚀 --- COMMENT --- @eslam-ahmed43 this issue is already team assigned.

n8n Cloud Support Ticket — HighLevel OAuth2 token exchange fails silently

Subject: HighLevel OAuth2 credential — authorization succeeds at GoHighLevel, oauthTokenData never populates (related to open issue #24073)

Summary

The HighLevel OAuth2 API credential on my n8n Cloud instance completes authorization successfully on GoHighLevel's side — the app installs onto the target location — but the token exchange at https://oauth.n8n.cloud/oauth2/callback never persists a token back to the credential. The credential permanently reports "Connect your account to use this credential."

This appears to be the same defect reported in open issue #24073.

Environment

Field | Value -- | -- n8n instance | treypound.app.n8n.cloud Plan | Cloud Credential ID | 5hhQ2WxuWjNWhPYZ Credential name | HighLevel account Credential type | highLevelOAuth2Api Workflow | Tailormade AI - Lead Qualification & Routing (eRKkThvWY4xovR1x) Node | Update GoHighLevel Contact (n8n-nodes-base.highLevel, operation: contact/update) Date observed | 25 July 2026

Ruled out

  • Redirect URI mismatch — byte-for-byte identical on both sides, and set as default in GHL
  • Wrong or inactive client key — correct pair confirmed and set as Default
  • App not published — app is Live v1.0.0, not Draft
  • Wrong distribution type — Private / Sub-Account, matching the target
  • Stale OAuth state — reproduced on a single clean click with a fresh session and no other windows open
  • Expired n8n session — re-authenticated immediately before the final attempt

Requests

  1. Please check server-side logs for the token exchange attempts on credential 5hhQ2WxuWjNWhPYZ (25 July 2026) — the failure is silent client-side, so the cause is only visible in your logs.
  2. Is there a known incompatibility between oauth.n8n.cloud/oauth2/callback and GoHighLevel's token endpoint (e.g. content-type, user_type, or form-encoding expectations)?
  3. Is there an ETA on issue #24073, or a supported workaround for n8n Cloud users?

Impact

This blocks the native HighLevel node entirely on n8n Cloud. Proceeding with GoHighLevel Private Integration Tokens via HTTP Request nodes as an interim workaround, which forfeits the native node's resource-locator field pickers. Would prefer to migrate back to the native node once resolved.

title: Support Application Default Credentials (auto-detect) for GCP Secrets Manager external secrets provider
thread_text:
TITLE:
Support Application Default Credentials (auto-detect) for GCP Secrets Manager external secrets provider

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The GCP Secrets Manager external secrets provider (`packages/cli/src/modules/external-secrets.ee/providers/gcp-secrets-manager/gcp-secrets-manager.ts`) only accepts a pasted service account JSON key (`client_email` + `private_key`). There's no way to use Application Default Credentials — e.g. GKE Workload Identity Federation, or `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`/metadata-server-based auth.

This is inconsistent with the AWS Secrets Manager provider, which already supports an `authMethod` field with two options: `iamUser` (static access key/secret) and `autoDetect` (AWS SDK default credential provider chain — env vars, IAM roles, instance/container profiles). Static, long-lived JSON keys are a known security anti-pattern for GCP service accounts and are exactly what an external-secrets feature should help teams move away from.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add an `authMethod` option to the GCP Secrets Manager provider config, mirroring the AWS provider's pattern:
- `serviceAccountKey` (current behavior) — paste JSON key, unchanged.
- `autoDetect` — omit `credentials` when constructing `SecretManagerServiceClient`, letting `@google-cloud/secret-manager` fall back to Application Default Credentials (metadata server / Workload Identity Federation on GKE, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` env var elsewhere).

`project_id` would still need to be supplied explicitly (or optionally auto-detected from the metadata server, same as the GCP client libraries support).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Rotating the service account key on a schedule via the public API. Works but keeps a long-lived credential in play and adds operational overhead the feature is otherwise meant to eliminate.

title: pagination expression referencing $request sends masked credential placeholder instead of real value
thread_text:
TITLE:
pagination expression referencing $request sends masked credential placeholder instead of real value

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
### Bug Description

### Bug Description

The HTTP Request node exposes a `$request` object to pagination expressions (used in "Next URL" and "Update a Parameter in Each Request" pagination modes). For security, any credential-bearing field on `$request` (e.g. `headers.Authorization`) is masked with the placeholder string `**hidden**` before the expression can read it — see `sanitizeUiMessage()` in `packages/nodes-base/nodes/HttpRequest/GenericFunctions.ts`.

If a pagination expression reads one of those masked fields and forwards it into the next request (e.g. `{{$request.headers.Authorization}}`, a natural thing to try when building cursor/header-based pagination for an API), the literal string `**hidden**` is sent as the real header value instead of the actual credential. This silently breaks authentication on page 2 onward with a confusing failure (typically a 401 from the third-party API), rather than a clear n8n-side error explaining what went wrong.

This was found while investigating #16005, which is a separate, broader bug (auth being dropped entirely during pagination for generic credential types, already covered by open PR #25470) — this issue is specifically about users who try to manually carry `$request` fields forward into their pagination configuration.

### To Reproduce

1. Create an HTTP Request node with Bearer Auth (Generic Credential Type) configured
2. Enable pagination, mode "Update a Parameter in Each Request"
3. Add a parameter of type "Headers" with name `Authorization` and value set to the expression `{{$request.headers.Authorization}}`
4. Execute the node against an API that requires the Authorization header on every paginated request

### Expected behavior

Either the real Authorization header value is forwarded (not possible without exposing the raw secret to the expression engine), or n8n throws a clear, actionable error telling the user that authenticated fields are already included in every paginated request automatically and must not be read back out of `$request`.

title: AWS S3 - headers[headerName].trim is not a function
thread_text:
TITLE:
AWS S3 - headers[headerName].trim is not a function

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
<!-- Please follow the template below. Skip the questions that are not relevant to you. -->

## Describe the problem/error/question

After our n8n Cloud instance auto-updated to 2.30.7, every workflow step that uploads a file to Amazon S3 fails during request signing. Nothing in the workflow or the credential changed — only the n8n Cloud version did — so this looks like a regression in the 2.30.x line.

Crucially, the failure is not specific to the AWS S3 node. It also happens with the generic HTTP Request node when it uses the AWS Predefined Credential Type to sign a request that carries a body (PUT/POST). Both fail with the exact same error at the same location in n8n-core: requestWithAuthentication at authentication.ts:263. This strongly indicates the problem is in the shared credential-authenticated request path, not in either node.

Observed facts

AWS S3 node (typeVersion 2, latest), operation Upload → fails.
HTTP Request node (typeVersion 4.2), method PUT, binary body, Authentication = Predefined Credential Type = AWS → fails with the identical error and the same core stack frame.
The AWS S3 node configuration is minimal (bucket + destination key only — no metadata, no tags, no custom headers), so no user expression is injecting a non-string header value.
No workflow or credential change was made. The only change was the automatic Cloud update.
The same uploads worked on the previous version.

Root-cause hypothesis (unverified, for maintainers)

At authentication.ts:263, requestWithAuthentication appears to call .trim() on header values while normalizing/signing the request headers. On a request that carries a body, at least one header value is a number rather than a string — the auto-generated Content-Length is the prime candidate — and .trim() is not a function on a number, hence the TypeError. Earlier versions presumably coerced header values to strings (or did not trim them), which would explain why this only started after the update. A defensive String(value).trim() (or skipping non-string values) at that location would likely fix it.

Impact

This breaks every authenticated AWS request that sends a body (i.e. all S3 uploads), via both the dedicated node and the generic HTTP Request node. There is therefore no node-level workaround while staying on this version.

title: OAuth consent fails with "Invalid or expired authorization session" - n8n-oauth-session cookie hardcoded with Secure attribute ignoring N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false
thread_text:
TITLE:
OAuth consent fails with "Invalid or expired authorization session" - n8n-oauth-session cookie hardcoded with Secure attribute ignoring N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
### Bug Description

When running n8n over plain HTTP with N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false set, the OAuth/MCP consent flow fails. The n8n-oauth-session cookie is still being set with the Secure attribute regardless of this setting. Browsers silently drop Secure cookies on non-HTTPS origins, so the session cookie never gets stored. The subsequent request to /rest/consent/details then fails a browserId check, returning a generic "Invalid or expired authorization session" error, making it impossible to complete OAuth/MCP authorization on an HTTP-only n8n instance.

Confirmed workaround: putting n8n behind an HTTPS reverse proxy (e.g. Caddy) resolves the issue immediately, since the cookie is honored once the origin is actually secure. This should not be required when N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false is explicitly set, since that env var is documented as the way to disable Secure-cookie behavior for HTTP deployments.

### To Reproduce

1. Run n8n in Docker with N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false and N8N_PROTOCOL=http (plain HTTP, no reverse proxy)
2. 2. Enable Instance-level MCP under Settings
3. 3. Configure an MCP client (e.g. Claude Desktop via mcp-remote) to connect via OAuth to http://<host>:5678/mcp-server/http
4. 4. Start the OAuth flow and approve the consent screen when it appears
5. 5. Observe the flow fails with "Invalid or expired authorization session" instead of completing
6. 6. Inspect cookies in the browser: n8n-oauth-session is present in the Set-Cookie response header with the Secure attribute, but is never actually stored by the browser because the connection is HTTP, not HTTPS

### Expected behavior

The OAuth consent flow should complete successfully when N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false is set on an HTTP-only instance, since that setting is documented as the way to allow the session cookie to work without HTTPS. The n8n-oauth-session cookie should be issued without the Secure attribute in this configuration so browsers actually store it, allowing /rest/consent/details to pass its browserId check.

title: JavaScript task runner cannot resolve allowlisted external npm modules in custom runners image
thread_text:
TITLE:
JavaScript task runner cannot resolve allowlisted external npm modules in custom runners image

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
### Bug Description

I spent some time debugging the JavaScript task runner implementation before opening this issue.

From my investigation:

The allowlist configuration is being applied correctly.
The task runner accepts the allowlisted module.
The failure happens only when resolving the module via require().
This suggests that the issue is related to dependency resolution rather than allowlist validation.

Before working on a potential fix and submitting a PR, I'd like to understand whether this is an unintended bug or an intentional design decision. If this is expected behavior for security reasons, I won't pursue a code change and will instead look at improving the documentation or developer experience.

If this is considered a bug, I'd be happy to work on a fix and submit a pull request.

### To Reproduce

1. Deploy n8n v2.30.8 with External Task Runners using Docker Compose.
2. Configure n8n-task-runners.json to allow an external module:
{
 "javascript": {
 "allowedBuiltInModules": ["crypto"],
 "allowedExternalModules": ["jsonwebtoken"]
 }
}
3. Mount the configuration into the runners container:
volumes:
 - ./n8n-task-runners.json:/etc/n8n-task-runners.json:ro

4. Create a Code (JavaScript) node:
const jwt = require("jsonwebtoken");

return [
 {
 token: jwt.sign({ hello: "world" }, "secret")
 }
];
Execute the workflow.

### Expected behavior

ince jsonwebtoken is explicitly allowlisted, the JavaScript task runner should be able to resolve and import the module when it is available in the runner image.

If the module resolution mechanism intentionally does not support dependencies added to a custom ghcr.io/n8n-io/runners image, the documentation should clearly state this limitation.

Actual behavior

The task runner accepts the allowlist configuration but fails during module resolution.

Initially the error is:

Module 'jsonwebtoken' is disallowed

After updating n8n-task-runners.json to allow the module, the error changes to:

Allowlisted module 'jsonwebtoken' is not installed.

and eventually:

Cannot find module 'jsonwebtoken'

Require stack:
- /opt/runners/task-runner-javascript/dist/js-task-runner/require-resolver.js
- /opt/runners/task-runner-javascript/dist/js-task-runner/js-task-runner.js
- /opt/runners/task-runner-javascript/dist/start.js

This indicates that the allowlist is working, but dependency resolution is failing.

### Debug Info

Before opening this issue, I investigated the implementation to better understand the behavior.

What I found
allowedExternalModules is correctly loaded from n8n-task-runners.json.
The error changes from "Module is disallowed" to "Cannot find module", which suggests the allowlist is being applied correctly.
The failure occurs during require() inside:
/opt/runners/task-runner-javascript/dist/js-task-runner/require-resolver.js
The JavaScript task runner eventually calls:
require(request)

and Node.js cannot resolve the module.

Because of this, it is unclear whether:

this is an unintended bug in the module resolution logic, or
loading third-party npm packages from a custom runners image is intentionally unsupported.

If this is considered a bug, I'd be happy to investigate further and submit a PR.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 LTS

### n8n Version

2.30.8

### Node.js Version

24.x (official Docker image) :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

### Database

PostgreSQL

title: Regression: Human Review approval does not execute the wrapped AI Tool in n8n 2.27.5, but works in 2.6.0
thread_text:
TITLE:
Regression: Human Review approval does not execute the wrapped AI Tool in n8n 2.27.5, but works in 2.6.0

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
### Bug Description

The native Human-in-the-Loop approval flow for AI tools does not behave correctly in n8n 2.27.5.

I created a minimal workflow in which the `Calculator` AI Tool is protected by a `Chat - Human Review` node before being exposed to the `AI Agent`.

The intended topology is:

```text
Calculator
 |
 | ai_tool
 v
Chat - Human Review
 |
 | ai_tool
 v
AI Agent
```

The AI Agent also uses a Chat Model:

```text
Ollama Chat Model
 |
 | ai_languageModel
 v
AI Agent
```

The main workflow is:

```text
When chat message received
 |
 | main
 v
AI Agent
 |
 | main
 v
Chat - Send Message
```

In n8n 2.6.0, this setup works correctly.

In n8n 2.27.5, the AI Agent generates the Calculator tool call and the Human Review approval UI is shown. However, after clicking `Approve`, the wrapped Calculator tool is either not executed or its real result is not returned to the AI Agent.

The agent receives only the approval response, for example:

```json
[
 {
 "data": {
 "approved": true
 }
 }
]
```

Instead of receiving the real Calculator result:

```text
40
```

Because the agent never receives the real tool result, it may retry the model/tool call until reaching the configured maximum number of iterations.

This appears to be a regression in the native Human Review tool wrapper or in the workflow resume behavior after approval.

### To Reproduce

1. Start a self-hosted n8n instance using version `2.27.5`.

2. Create a new workflow.

3. Add a `When chat message received` node.

4. Configure the Chat Trigger with:

```text
Response Mode: Using Response Nodes
```

5. Connect the Chat Trigger to an `AI Agent`.

6. Connect an Ollama Chat Model to the `ai_languageModel` input of the AI Agent.

7. Add a `Calculator` AI Tool.

8. Add a `Chat - Human Review` node.

9. Connect the nodes using this exact topology:

```text
Calculator
 |
 | ai_tool
 v
Chat - Human Review
 |
 | ai_tool
 v
AI Agent
```

10. Configure the Human Review node with:

```text
Approval Type: Approve and Disapprove
```

11. Add a final `Chat - Send Message` node after the AI Agent.

12. Configure the final Chat node with:

```text
Message: {{ $json.output }}
```

13. Configure the AI Agent with:

```text
Max Iterations: 4
Return Intermediate Steps: enabled
```

14. Use this system message:

```text
You are a minimal Human-in-the-Loop tool approval test agent.

When the user's message starts with `TEST:`:

1. Extract the arithmetic expression that follows `TEST:`.
2. Call the `Calculator` tool exactly once.
3. Do not calculate the expression yourself.
4. Do not invent, estimate, or assume a tool result.
5. Call only one tool at a time and wait for its actual result.

After an approved Calculator call with a valid result, respond exactly with:

TOOL_APPROVED | result=<real result>

If the tool execution is rejected, denied, or cancelled, do not call the Calculator again in the same turn.

Respond exactly with:

TOOL_DISAPPROVED | calculator was not executed.

If no real Calculator result is received, respond exactly with:

TOOL_FAILED | no real calculator result received.

For any other message, respond exactly with:

Send `TEST: <arithmetic expression>`.
```

15. Open the n8n chat and send:

```text
TEST: 17+23
```

16. Confirm that the AI Agent generates a Calculator tool call similar to:

```json
{
 "tool": "Calculator",
 "toolParameters": {
 "input": "17+23"
 }
}
```

17. Click `Approve` in the Human Review message.

### Expected behavior

After clicking `Approve`:

1. The Human Review node should resume the execution.
2. The wrapped `Calculator` tool should execute exactly once.
3. The Calculator should receive:

```text
17+23
```

4. The Calculator should return:

```text
40
```

5. The real Calculator result should be passed back to the AI Agent as the tool observation.
6. The AI Agent should generate the final response:

```text
TOOL_APPROVED | result=40
```

The expected execution order is:

```text
Ollama Chat Model
Chat - Human Review
Calculator
Ollama Chat Model
Chat - Send Message
```

# Actual behavior

The Human Review approval message is displayed correctly.

After clicking `Approve`, the approval response is returned, but the Calculator result is not returned to the agent.

The intermediate step may contain only:

```json
{
 "data": {
 "approved": true
 }
}
```

instead of:

```text
40
```

In some executions, the Calculator node does not appear in the execution trace at all.

The agent then continues calling the Chat Model until it reaches the maximum number of iterations.

Example error:

```text
Max iterations reached. The agent could not complete the task within the allowed number of iterations.
```

### Debug Info

# Version comparison

## Works correctly

```text
n8n 2.6.0
```

## Does not work correctly

```text
n8n 2.27.5
```

# Environment

```text
Deployment: Self-hosted Docker
Affected n8n version: 2.27.5
Working n8n version: 2.6.0
Operating system: Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)
Browser: Firefox
Chat Trigger response mode: Using Response Nodes
AI Agent node version: 3 / 3.1
Human Review node type: @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.chatHitlTool
Human Review node version: 1.3
Tool: Calculator
Chat Model: Ollama Chat Model
Database: SQLite or PostgreSQL
```

# Additional information

The model appears to generate a valid tool call.

Example:

```json
{
 "tool": "Calculator",
 "toolParameters": {
 "input": "17+23"
 }
}
```

The problem appears to happen after the approval response is submitted.

The Human Review node returns the approval result as the tool observation:

```json
{
 "approved": true
}
```

However, the wrapped Calculator tool does not appear to run afterward, or its output is not forwarded back to the AI Agent.

Could you please confirm whether this is a known regression and whether there is a fix or supported workaround that preserves this exact topology?

```text
Calculator -> Human Review -> AI Agent
```

I specifically need the Human Review node to remain between the AI Agent and the protected tool, rather than moving the approval step into the main workflow path.

### Operating System

Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)

### n8n Version

2.27.5

### Node.js Version

24.16.0

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

title: [Bug]: n8n v2.30.7 hangs after DB migrations on Windows (Node 24) — all routes return 404
thread_text:
TITLE:
[Bug]: n8n v2.30.7 hangs after DB migrations on Windows (Node 24) — all routes return 404

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
## Bug Description

A fresh installation of `n8n@2.30.7` (via `npm install -g n8n@latest`) starts successfully but only the `/healthz` endpoint works. All other routes (Web UI at `/`, REST API at `/rest/settings`, `/rest/owner`, `/api/v1/workflows`, etc.) return **404 `Cannot GET ...`**.

The server logs `"n8n ready on ::, port 8080"` and the health check responds `{"status":"ok"}`, but the web application routes are never registered.

## Root Cause Analysis

The new `@Command` decorator framework in n8n v2.30.x uses a two-phase lifecycle:

1. **`command.init()`** — initializes DB, starts HTTP server (logs "n8n ready")
2. **`command.run()`** — calls `this.server.start()` → `AbstractServer.start()` → `await this.configure()` → **`ControllerRegistry.activate(app)`** (registers all routes)

The `init()` method hangs **after DB migrations complete**, somewhere in the post-migration initialization within `BaseCommand.init()`. Because `init()` never resolves, `run()` is never called, and therefore:
- `server.start()` is never called
- `configure()` never runs
- `ControllerRegistry.activate(app)` never registers routes
- Only the health endpoint (set up in `AbstractServer.init()`) is available

### Evidence from process output

With the original database (already migrated), the last output from the process is:

```
Finished migration CreateSchedulerTables1784000000042
```

After that, the process remains running for over 4 minutes with no further output and the process never displays `"Editor is now accessible via:"` which comes from `Start.run()`.

### Suspected hang point

The most likely hang is in `TaskRunnerModule.start()` (called from `BaseCommand.init()` after DB migration), which attempts to spawn JS and Python task runner child processes via `startInternalTaskRunners()`. This could also be in `PostHogClient.init()` if the telemetry server is unreachable.

## To Reproduce

1. Install Node.js v24.16.0 on Windows 10
2. Run `npm install -g n8n@2.30.7`
3. Run `n8n start --port=8080`
4. Wait for `"n8n ready on ::, port 8080"` message
5. Try `curl http://localhost:8080/` — returns 404

## Expected behavior

All routes should be registered after the server starts. The Web UI and REST API should be accessible.

## Environment

- **n8n Version:** 2.30.7
- **Node.js Version:** v24.16.0
- **OS:** Windows 10
- **Database:** SQLite (default)
- **npm install:** global (`npm install -g n8n@latest`)

## Debug Info

Workaround attempted: Patching `dist/commands/start.js` to wrap the initial database query in `run()` with try/catch had no effect, confirming the hang is in `init()`, not `run()`.

Note: This is a **different bug** from issue #33370 (the @langchain/core exports crash in v2.28.x). The langchain bug is fixed in v2.30.7, but this new startup hang prevents the server from serving any routes.

title: Instance-level MCP OAuth: token exchange fails with "code_verifier does not match the challenge" (InvalidGrantError) after successful consent
thread_text:
TITLE:
Instance-level MCP OAuth: token exchange fails with "code_verifier does not match the challenge" (InvalidGrantError) after successful consent

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
### Bug Description

Connecting to n8n's Instance-level MCP server from Claude Desktop (via mcp-remote) consistently fails at the token-exchange step of the OAuth flow, even though Dynamic Client Registration, the authorize redirect, and consent all succeed.

mcp-remote's client log shows:
"Authorization error: InvalidGrantError: code_verifier does not match the challenge"
immediately after "Completing authorization...".

Server-side, n8n's debug logs (N8N_LOG_LEVEL=debug) show "Starting OAuth authorization" and "Consent approved" entries, but nothing at all for the subsequent token exchange request/response - no log line, no error, no warning - suggesting the PKCE code_verifier/code_challenge comparison happens in a lower-level OAuth library that isn't covered by n8n's own logging.

This reproduces 100% of the time, and we have ruled out the usual suspects:
- Stale client-side auth cache: cleared mcp-remote's .mcp-auth folder, confirmed a fresh client_id was issued on the next attempt - same error.
- - Reverse-proxy header issues: set N8N_PROXY_HOPS=1 (we were previously seeing express-rate-limit ValidationError: X-Forwarded-For header is set but trust proxy is false); after the fix those errors disappeared entirely, but the PKCE error persisted.
- - - Competing mcp-remote processes on the callback port: reproduced with a single, clean process (no EADDRINUSE, no port conflicts) - still fails identically.
This is a separate, still-unreported issue from #34955 (which was about the n8n-oauth-session cookie hardcoding Secure) - that issue is fixed/filed separately, and this PKCE failure persists independently of it.

### To Reproduce

1. Enable Instance-level MCP on a self-hosted n8n instance running behind an HTTPS reverse proxy (Caddy in our case), with N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=true and N8N_PROXY_HOPS=1 set.
2. 2. Configure Claude Desktop's config to use mcp-remote pointed at https://<host>/mcp-server/http, with a fixed callback port (8090) and auth timeout 120s.
3. 3. Launch Claude Desktop. It opens a browser window to n8n's OAuth consent screen (authorize request includes a valid code_challenge/code_challenge_method=S256).
4. 4. Approve consent (click Allow).
5. 5. Observe mcp-remote's log: it receives the auth code and immediately fails while "Completing authorization..." with "InvalidGrantError: code_verifier does not match the challenge".
6. 6. Repeat with N8N_LOG_LEVEL=debug set on the n8n container: server logs show "Starting OAuth authorization" and "Consent approved" but no log entry at all for the token exchange request/response itself.

### Expected behavior

The token exchange should succeed using the same code_verifier/code_challenge pair generated for the original /mcp-oauth/authorize request, and Claude Desktop should connect to the Instance-level MCP server successfully after consent is approved.

### Debug Info

n8nVersion: 2.31.6
platform: docker (self-hosted)
nodeJsVersion: 24.16.0
nodeEnv: production
database: sqlite (default)
executionMode: main (default)
hosting: self-hosted, Docker container, behind a Caddy HTTPS reverse proxy
relevant env vars: N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=true, N8N_PROXY_HOPS=1, N8N_HOST, WEBHOOK_URL and N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL set to the HTTPS proxy URL
MCP client: Claude Desktop (Windows), using mcp-remote via npx, fixed callback port 8090, --auth-timeout 120

### Operating System

Debian 12 (Proxmox LXC host); n8n container based on Alpine Linux

### n8n Version

2.31.6

### Node.js Version

24.16.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

DISCUSSION:
Hey @jeremyhboss,

Thank you for reaching out! We’ve received your issue and are looking into it. To help us track this internally, we’ve created a Linear ticket with the reference: "GHC-9095".

We’ll keep you updated as we make progress, but if you have any additional details or context to share, feel free to add them here - it’s always helpful!

Thanks for your patience and for bringing this to our attention.

---
> For *INTERNAL* use only: [GHC-9095](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/GHC-9095)

--- COMMENT ---

Hi @jeremyhboss, thanks for the thorough report. We've traced what this error can and cannot mean on the server side, and that narrows things down a lot.

code_verifier does not match the challenge is only returned when the authorization code itself is valid: it exists, is unexpired, unused, and belongs to your client_id. The only way to hit it is when the code was created from a different authorization attempt than the one your mcp-remote process is waiting on. In other words, two OAuth authorization flows ran against the same server around the same time and overwrote each other's state (n8n keeps the pending authorization in a single browser cookie, and mcp-remote keeps a single code_verifier.txt per server URL, so a second flow silently replaces both). Claude Desktop on Windows is known to spawn each configured MCP server twice at startup (anthropics/claude-code#53134), which produces exactly this pattern, and mcp-remote's lockfile coordination avoids the EADDRINUSE you checked for, so a second instance can be present without a port conflict.

To confirm, could you check the following:

1. Count the processes. While Claude Desktop is running, check Task Manager for multiple node/npx processes running mcp-remote for this server (or run wmic process where "commandline like '%mcp-remote%'" get processid,commandline in a terminal).
2. Check the MCP log for duplicate auth flows. In Claude Desktop's logs/mcp-server-<name>.log, look for the phrase Please authorize this client by visiting appearing more than once per connection attempt, and note whether your browser opened (or you clicked) more than one consent tab.
3. Run mcp-remote debug mode. Add --debug to the mcp-remote args and retry; it writes ~/.mcp-auth/<hash>_debug.log, which records every code_verifier save/read and will show if a second flow overwrote the first one's verifier.
4. Test outside Claude Desktop. With Claude Desktop fully closed, clear .mcp-auth, then run a single instance manually in one terminal: npx -y mcp-remote@latest https://<host>/mcp-server/http 8090, and approve the consent. If this succeeds, the server-side flow (including your proxy setup) is fine and the problem is the duplicated client processes.
5. Be logged into n8n before you start. If the consent screen takes a while (for example a login redirect first), a second mcp-remote instance can time out waiting and start its own competing flow. Being pre-authenticated and approving promptly avoids that window.

TITLE:
MCP tool update_workflow does not support setting availableInMCP via setWorkflowSettings

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
### Bug Description

When using the n8n MCP server's `update_workflow` tool with a `setWorkflowSettings` operation to set `availableInMCP`, the operation is rejected with the error: "settings must specify at least one field".

This is related to but distinct from #27803 (which was fixed in 2.17.0 for the classic REST API `PUT /api/v1/workflows/{id}` endpoint). The only working method is manually toggling "Available in MCP" in the workflow's Settings menu in the n8n editor UI.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow via the MCP server using `create_workflow_from_code`. This automatically sets `availableInMCP: true`.
2. Attempt to set it back to `false` using the `update_workflow` MCP tool with an operation like:
 { "type": "setWorkflowSettings", "settings": { "availableInMCP": false } }
3. The MCP server rejects the operation with: "settings must specify at least one field"
4. Confirm via `get_workflow_details` (MCP) that `availableInMCP` remains `true`, or manually check the workflow's Settings in the n8n editor UI.

### Expected behavior

The `update_workflow` MCP tool's `setWorkflowSettings` operation should accept `availableInMCP` as a valid field, allowing MCP clients to enable or disable MCP exposure programmatically — consistent with the fix already applied to the classic REST API in #27803.

title: Google Service Account Impersonation failing validation (but working)
thread_text: TITLE: Google Service Account Impersonation failing validation (but working) ISSUE DESCRIPTION: ### Bug Description ## Title `googleApi` credential test always requests hardcoded Google **Sheets** scopes, so it can never pass with "Impersonate a User" enabled unless the domain granted Sheets/Drive scopes. ## Description The **Google Service Account API** (`googleApi`) credential is shared across Calendar, BigQuery, Chat, Vertex, Gmail, Drive, Sheets and the HTTP Request node. Its **Test** button always authenticates using the hardcoded `sheetV2` scope set, ignoring the credential's own `Scope(s)` field. With **Impersonate a User** OFF this is invisible: `sub` is the service account itself, so it is a plain two-legged JWT flow with no domain-wide-delegation check, and Google issues a token for essentially any scope. The test goes green while proving nothing. With **Impersonate a User** ON, `sub` becomes the delegated user, Google performs the DWD authorization check - against **Sheets/Drive scopes the user never asked for** - and returns: ```sh Private key validation failed: 401 - {"error":"unauthorized_client", "error_description":"Client is unauthorized to retrieve access tokens using this method, or client not authorized for any of the scopes requested."} ``` For anyone using this credential for a non-Sheets service, the test is **structurally incapable of passing**. My case: Google Calendar via the HTTP Request node, DWD granted for `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly` only. ## Analysis (claude) `googleApi` declares no `test` of its own. Its only `testedBy` binding is contributed by the Google Sheets node: **[`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Sheet/v2/actions/versionDescription.ts#L77-L84`](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n%402.32.5/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Sheet/v2/actions/versionDescription.ts#L77-L84)** ```ts name: 'googleApi', ... testedBy: 'googleApiCredentialTest', ``` **[`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Sheet/v2/methods/credentialTest.ts#L14`](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n%402.32.5/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Sheet/v2/methods/credentialTest.ts#L14)** ```ts const tokenRequest = await getGoogleAccessToken.call(this, credential.data!, 'sheetV2'); // ^^^^^^^^^ ``` **[`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/GenericFunctions.ts#L43-L47`](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n%402.32.5/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/GenericFunctions.ts#L43-L47)** ```ts sheetV2: [ 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file', 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets', 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.metadata', ], ``` **[`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/GenericFunctions.ts#L87-L98`](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n%402.32.5/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/GenericFunctions.ts#L87-L98)** ```ts const scopes = googleServiceAccountScopes[service]; // ← 'sheetV2', always ... const signature = jwt.sign({ iss: credentials.email, sub: credentials.delegatedEmail || credentials.email, // ← impersonation toggles the DWD check scope: scopes.join(' '), // ← user's Scope(s) field never read aud: 'https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token', ``` Meanwhile the credential's **runtime** signer does read the user's field: **[`packages/nodes-base/credentials/GoogleApi.credentials.ts#L330-L347`](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n%402.32.5/packages/nodes-base/credentials/GoogleApi.credentials.ts#L330-L347)** ```ts async authenticate(credentials, requestOptions) { if (!credentials.httpNode) return requestOptions; const credentialsScopes = (credentials.scopes as string).replace(/\\n/g, '\n').trim(); ... sub: credentials.delegatedEmail || credentials.email, scope: scopes, // ← the user's Scope(s) field ``` **So the test and the runtime disagree about what this credential is for.** The runtime is right; the test is wrong. ### To Reproduce 1. Create a GCP service account, download the JSON key, enable **Google Calendar API**. 2. Admin console → Security → API controls → **Domain-wide delegation** → authorize the SA's client ID for exactly `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly`. 3. n8n → Credentials → **Google Service Account API**: - Service Account Email + Private Key from the JSON - **Set up for use in HTTP Request node** = ON - Scope(s) = `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly` - **Impersonate a User** = OFF → **Test passes** (misleadingly) 4. Set **Impersonate a User** = ON, Email = a real Workspace user → **Test fails** with `unauthorized_client`. 5. Save anyway and use it from an HTTP Request node against `GET https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{id}/events` → **works correctly**. ### Expected behavior The test should validate the scopes the credential is actually configured for. Specifically: when `httpNode` is true, request `credentials.scopes` rather than `sheetV2`. Failing that, the credential should not advertise a test it cannot satisfy, or should surface *which* scopes it just tried so the error is diagnosable. At minimum, include the attempted scopes in the failure message - the current text (`Private key validation failed`) points at the private key, which is the one thing that is not wrong, and sends everyone down a PEM-formatting rabbit hole. ### Debug Info # Debug info ## core - n8nVersion: 2.32.5 - platform: docker (self-hosted) - nodeJsVersion: 24.18.0 - nodeEnv: production - database: postgres - executionMode: regular - concurrency: -1 - license: community - consumerId: unknown ## storage - success: all - error: all - progress: false - manual: true - binaryMode: filesystem ## pruning - enabled: true - maxAge: 336 hours - maxCount: 10000 executions ## client - userAgent: mozilla/5.0 (x11; linux x86_64) applewebkit/537.36 (khtml, like gecko) chrome/150.0.0.0 safari/537.36 - isTouchDevice: false ## security - secureCookie: false ## cluster - instanceCount: 1 - versions: 2.32.5 - instances: - instanceKey: f82d3042-a816-4111-9aa8-45ec5c54d583, hostId: main-bbbf9c8856f0, instanceType: main, instanceRole: leader, version: 2.32.5 - checks: - check: hostid-clash, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: lifecycle, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: split-brain, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: version-mismatch, status: succeeded, warnings: - Generated at: 2026-07-26T06:56:09.602Z ### Operating System Ubuntu Linux 24.04 ### n8n Version 2.32.5 ### Node.js Version 24 ### Database PostgreSQL ### Execution mode main (default) ### Hosting self hosted

title: Salesforce node (OAuth2): refresh silently drops oauthTokenData.instance_url, causing "Invalid URL" (ERR_INVALID_URL) until manual reconnect
thread_text:
TITLE:
Salesforce node (OAuth2): refresh silently drops oauthTokenData.instance_url, causing "Invalid URL" (ERR_INVALID_URL) until manual reconnect

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
### Bug Description

Self-hosted n8n (queue mode, PostgreSQL). A workflow using the **Salesforce** node with a **Salesforce OAuth2 API** credential works fine for a period (intraday token refreshes succeed), then starts failing every execution with:

```
NodeApiError: Invalid URL
httpCode: ERR_INVALID_URL
```

Manually reconnecting the credential (full OAuth authorize flow) fixes it immediately - but it breaks again after the next background token refresh cycle, in a repeatable "works after reconnect, dies again after ~a day" pattern. Same Salesforce org, different dedicated integration user/Connected App works fine on a separate (dev) n8n instance running identical n8n version/config.

### Root Cause (traced from an actual failing execution)

`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Salesforce/GenericFunctions.ts` builds every API request URL from the credential's stored OAuth token data:

```ts
const credentials = await this.getCredentials<{ oauthTokenData: { instance_url: string } }>('salesforceOAuth2Api');
const options = getOptions.call(this, method, uri || endpoint, body, qs,
 credentials.oauthTokenData.instance_url);
...
uri: `${instanceUrl}/services/data/${SALESFORCE_API_VERSION}${endpoint}`
```

When `oauthTokenData.instance_url` is empty/undefined, this produces something like `"undefined/services/data/v59.0/..."`, which Node's `URL` parser rejects with `ERR_INVALID_URL` - exactly the error surfaced to the user, with a stack trace rooted at `GenericFunctions.ts:192` (`salesforceApiRequest`).

The reason `instance_url` goes missing: `packages/core/src/execution-engine/node-execution-context/utils/request-helpers/oauth.ts`, in the generic OAuth2 token-refresh path, merges old and refreshed token data like this:

```ts
const newOAuthTokenData = addExpiresAt({ ...token.data, ...newToken.data });

// If the server doesn't echo the resource back, restore it from the
// previous token data to ensure it's not lost on refresh.
if (!newOAuthTokenData.resource && token.data.resource) {
 newOAuthTokenData.resource = token.data.resource;
}
```

There's an explicit, deliberate fallback to preserve **only** the `resource` field if the authorization server's refresh response doesn't echo it back. There is no equivalent protection for any other non-standard field a credential type may depend on - such as Salesforce's `instance_url`, which the Salesforce node requires on every request but which isn't part of the generic OAuth2 core.

If a refresh-grant response from the auth server ever omits `instance_url` (for whatever server-side reason - scope config, session policy, etc.), n8n has no fallback and the credential is left permanently missing `instance_url` in its stored `oauthTokenData` until a full manual reconnect (fresh authorization-code grant) repopulates it. Every Salesforce node call fails with "Invalid URL" in the meantime, regardless of whether the access/refresh token itself is otherwise valid.

This looks like the same underlying issue reported (without root cause) in #19945 - "Salesforce OAuth not working properly", which has multiple independent reporters describing the identical "fails once a day, only fixed by reconnect" symptom, unresolved since Sept 2025.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a Salesforce OAuth2 API credential (Connected App / External Client App, refresh token granted).
2. Use it in a Salesforce node in a scheduled workflow.
3. Let it run past the point where n8n performs a background OAuth2 token refresh.
4. If the refresh-grant response from Salesforce doesn't include `instance_url`, every subsequent Salesforce node call fails with `Invalid URL` / `ERR_INVALID_URL` until the credential is manually reconnected.

### Expected Behavior

`instance_url` (and arguably any other non-standard field the original token response provided, e.g. `id`, `signature`) should be preserved across a refresh the same way `resource` already is - i.e., in `oauth.ts`, fall back to the previous `oauthTokenData` value for these fields when the refresh response doesn't include them, rather than only doing this for `resource`.

### Environment

- n8n version: 2.30.4
- Execution mode: queue (main + workers)
- Database: PostgreSQL
- Hosting: self-hosted (Kubernetes/Helm)
- Credential type: Salesforce OAuth2 API (`salesforceOAuth2Api`)

title: Postgres workflow statistics rollup crashes when firstEvent is returned as a non-Date value
thread_text:
TITLE:
Postgres workflow statistics rollup crashes when firstEvent is returned as a non-Date value

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
### Bug Description

On PostgreSQL, the workflow statistics rollup assumes that the result of:

```sql
MIN("createdAt") AS "firstEvent"
```

is always a JavaScript `Date`:

```ts
firstEventMs: r.firstEvent.getTime(),
```

In some PostgreSQL deployments, the raw query result is returned as a string or another non-`Date` timestamp representation. The statistics rollup then repeatedly fails with:

```text
TypeError: r.firstEvent.getTime is not a function
 at WorkflowStatisticsRepository.rollupIncrements (...)
```

Because the rollup runs repeatedly, the same exception can recur every few seconds. In our deployment, memory usage continued increasing until Node.js reached its heap limit and the n8n container restarted.

This was first observed on n8n 2.30.7. The same unsafe conversion is still present in 2.31.4, 2.32.0, and the current `master` branch as of 2026-07-21.

### To Reproduce

1. Run self-hosted n8n with PostgreSQL.
2. Create a new workflow that has no existing workflow statistics row.
3. Execute the workflow in production for the first time, through a webhook or another production trigger.
4. Allow the workflow statistics rollup task to run.
5. When PostgreSQL returns `firstEvent` as a non-`Date` value, observe the recurring exception:

```text
TypeError: r.firstEvent.getTime is not a function
```

The problem is most visible on the first production success or failure because the rollup processes newly inserted statistics records.

The exact reproduction may depend on the PostgreSQL driver or timestamp parser configuration.

### Expected behavior

The statistics rollup should normalize the PostgreSQL timestamp representation before converting it to milliseconds.

The rollup should:

- create the workflow statistics counter and milestone;
- drain the pending statistics deltas;
- complete without recurring exceptions;
- avoid unbounded heap growth caused by repeatedly retrying the same failing rollup.

### Debug Info

- Deployment: Self-hosted Docker
- First affected version observed: n8n 2.30.7
- Source also confirmed affected in: 2.31.4, 2.32.0, and `master`
- Node.js: 24.16.0
- Database: PostgreSQL 18.4
- Execution mode: `main`
- Operating system: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

### Proposed fix

Normalize `firstEvent` before converting it to milliseconds:

```ts
firstEventMs: new Date(r.firstEvent).getTime(),
```

We applied this change to a custom image based on n8n 2.31.4 and verified it using a new production workflow. The rollup completed, the workflow statistics were materialized, and the pending delta queue drained successfully.

A regression test should cover a rollup row whose `firstEvent` value is an ISO timestamp string rather than a JavaScript `Date`.

TITLE:
Instance-level MCP (2.31.4): valid OAuth access token with correct audience rejected by MCP endpoint — Claude connector fails with McpAuthorizationError after successful consent

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
### Bug Description

## Bug Description

On a self-hosted n8n 2.31.4 (Docker, Postgres), connecting Claude (web and desktop, identical behavior) to the instance-level MCP server via OAuth fails at the very last step. Dynamic Client Registration succeeds, the consent screen appears, the user authorizes, the authorization code is exchanged and an access token is minted — and then the first authenticated request to /mcp-server/http is rejected. Claude surfaces: "Your account was authorized, but the integration rejected the credentials it just issued" (oauth_error=McpAuthorizationError, step=end_error).

The rejected token is provably correct on the audience dimension, which is why I believe this is a mint/verify asymmetry rather than a configuration issue.

## Evidence

1. Protected resource metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp-server/http` advertises:
 `"resource": "https://<host>/mcp-server/http"`
2. Decoded payload of a freshly minted access token from the `oauth_access_tokens` table:
 `{"sub":"<user-uuid>","aud":"https://<host>/mcp-server/http","client_id":"<client-uuid>","jti":"...","iat":...,"exp":...,"meta":{"isOAuth":true}}`
 The `aud` exactly equals the advertised resource. Note: the payload carries the user id in `sub` only; there is no `userId` claim and no `iss` claim.
3. `mcp-server-middleware.service.js` sets `expectedAudience = mcpProtectedResource.getResourceUrl()`, and `mcp-protected-resource.js` builds that as instance base URL + `MCP_RESOURCE_PATH ('/mcp-server/http')` — the same value as 1 and 2. So the JWT audience check cannot be the mismatch.
4. Suspected cause (from reading `oauth-token.service.js` in the shipped dist): `verifyOAuthAccessToken()` resolves the user via `authInfo.extra['userId']` and returns `reason: 'user_id_not_in_auth_info'` when absent. Since minted tokens only carry `sub`, mint and verify appear asymmetric.

## What I ruled out

- `N8N_MCP_BASE_URL`: tested unset, hostname-only, and full MCP URL — identical failure in all three. (Full URL is provably wrong anyway: `getResourceUrl()` appends `MCP_RESOURCE_PATH` again, producing a doubled path.)
- Reverse proxy: single public hostname, `N8N_PROXY_HOPS=1`, Cloudflare Access bypassed for `/mcp-server`, `/mcp-oauth` and `/.well-known` (verified reachable; unauthenticated GET on the MCP URL returns the expected 401 JSON).
- Client-side: Claude web and Claude desktop fail identically. Claude support flow references: ofid_a60bdd30db30b192, ofid_7f851851c1eda01b.
- DB state is clean: registrations, consents and access tokens are all present and well-formed.

## Related issues found along the way (secondary, but worth fixing)

- `POST /mcp-oauth/register` returns HTTP 500 (`server_error`) instead of a 4xx when the "Allowed OAuth Redirect URLs" setting is empty, and also when the registration payload omits `grant_types`/`response_types`. This cost significant diagnosis time because the real cause (empty allowlist) was masked by a generic 500.
- The root `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (without path suffix) returns a 404; only the path-suffixed variant exists.
- The registration/verification errors are not logged at all, even with `N8N_LOG_LEVEL=debug`.

## Environment

- n8n version: 2.31.4 (also relevant: upgraded from 2.26.6, DB migrations clean)
- Database: PostgreSQL 16
- Running via: Docker Compose, self-hosted, cloudflared in front, single hostname

Related prior art: #30500 (closed) fixed tokens being minted with a hardcoded aud that ignored the resource parameter. This report is the inverse case on 2.31.4: the minted aud now exactly matches the advertised resource, yet the MCP endpoint still rejects the token.

3. In Claude, add a custom connector with `https://<host>/mcp-server/http` and connect.

Ran all your probes. **I think we found the failing call: the `GET /mcp-server/http` listen stream hangs indefinitely.**

Per the streamable-HTTP spec the server should either open the SSE stream right away (200 + headers) or return 405 if the listen stream is unsupported; an indefinite hang is neither. If Claude opens this GET stream during connect, a client-side timeout there would surface exactly as "the integration rejected the credentials it just issued". This is now my prime suspect.

**2) Refresh grant replay:** two results.
- Without `client_secret`: 400 `invalid_client` ("Client secret is required").

**1) Tunnel logs:** probably unnecessary now that the failing call is identified, and SSE buffering by the tunnel can be ruled out since the POST SSE response passes through instantly. I can still run a cloudflared debug round if you want the exact request sequence Claude makes.

**Working theory:** DCR → consent → code exchange all succeed; Claude then opens (or attempts) the GET listen stream, which never responds; Claude times out and reports `McpAuthorizationError`. The GET handler hanging instead of returning 200 or 405 looks like the server-side bug to chase.

Hii! 

I independently reproduced this on my end: `POST /mcp-server/http` with a valid token returns 200 and a full initialize result, while `GET /mcp-server/http` with the same token hangs indefinitely (curl timeout, zero bytes). This confirms your causal chain exactly. And, after going through the code I can say:

### What is happening (briefly)

The `GET` handler in `mcp.controller.ts` calls `handleTransportRequest` without a body. The SDK's `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` in stateless mode (`sessionIdGenerator: undefined`) creates a `ReadableStream` that never gets closed, and the Node server listener waits forever for `done: true` that never comes. Hence, it hangs. `POST` works because the SDK processes the body and finishes the response cycle normally.

### Approach for the fix

**Short term: return 405 Method Not Allowed** on `GET` before entering the transport. This is spec-compliant (Streamable HTTP allows servers to decline the listen stream), stops the hang immediately, and unblocks all MCP clients since they can still use `POST` for request/response.

**Long term: full SSE streaming** behind a feature flag. This would need session management, an SSE connection registry, event bridging, heartbeats, backpressure handling, and multi-instance considerations. The architecture for this is well understood, but it is a 600-1000+ line feature that needs proper design review.

Even though, I believe the full streaming implementation is solid and scalable, but I guess the team would like to take this on internally as it as an architectural change (I'm happy to contribute btw, if the team agrees 😄) So, the 405 fix seems reasonable for now.

Looks like this has been assigned to the @n8n-io/adore team so, if anyone can guide me then It'd be great!

Thank You!

TITLE:
AWS S3: SignatureDoesNotMatch on object keys containing "=" or ":" (path signed un-encoded, sent percent-encoded) — regression in 2.31.5

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
<!-- Please follow the template below. Skip the questions that are not relevant to you. -->

## Describe the bug

Downloading an S3 object whose key contains `=` or `:` fails with `403 SignatureDoesNotMatch`. This affects **any** Hive-partitioned S3 layout — Amazon Marketing Cloud, Athena/Glue query output, Spark/EMR output — where keys look like:

```
workflow=my_workflow_id/schedule=adhoc/2026-07-23T19:30:45.513Z-my_workflow_id.csv
```

n8n appears to compute the SigV4 signature over the **un-encoded** request path but transmit the **percent-encoded** path. AWS canonicalises the request it actually receives, so the string-to-sign never matches.

Per RFC 3986, `=` and `:` are legal unencoded in a path segment, and the AWS SDKs do not encode them in S3 object keys — so the transmitted path is being over-encoded relative to what was signed.

**This is not limited to the AWS S3 node.** The S3 node (V1 *and* V2) and the HTTP Request node with an AWS predefined credential all fail identically, because all three funnel through `requestWithAuthentication` → the AWS credential's signer.

## Is this a regression?

**Yes.** Identical workflows, node, credential, bucket and key shape ran successfully for weeks on **2.29.8** and began failing on **2.31.5** with no user-side change. The instance is n8n Cloud and was auto-upgraded between those versions.

## To Reproduce

1. Put an object in an S3 bucket with a key containing `=` and `:`, e.g.
 `workflow=test_id/schedule=adhoc/2026-07-23T19:30:45.513Z-test_id.csv`
2. Add an **AWS S3** node → Resource: File → Operation: Download → set Bucket and that File Key, with a valid AWS credential.
3. Execute.

**Result:** `403 SignatureDoesNotMatch`.

**Control that passes:** the same credential against an operation whose canonical path has no special characters (e.g. Get Many / list on the bucket) succeeds — so the credential and secret are correct.

## Expected behavior

The object downloads. The signature should be computed over the same canonical URI that is transmitted.

## Actual behavior — evidence

Four tests, all with the **same credential**, in the same session. AWS's own `CanonicalRequest` (from the 403 body) is the key evidence:

| # | Setup | SignedHeaders | Canonical path AWS saw | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | S3 node — list bucket | `host;x-amz-content-sha256;x-amz-date` | `/` | **PASS** |
| B | S3 node **V1** — download | `host;x-amz-content-sha256;x-amz-date` | `/workflow%3D…/…T19%3A30%3A45…csv` | FAIL |
| C | S3 node **V2** — download | `host;x-amz-content-sha256;x-amz-date` | `/workflow%3D…/…T19%3A30%3A45…csv` | FAIL |
| D | HTTP Request + AWS cred, virtual-hosted URL | — | — | FAIL, different error (see below) |
| E | HTTP Request + AWS cred, path-style URL | `accept;host;x-amz-content-sha256;x-amz-date` | `/bucket/workflow%3D…/…T19%3A30%3A45…csv` | FAIL |
| F | As E, but key **pre-percent-encoded** by the user | `accept;host;x-amz-content-sha256;x-amz-date` | same | **PASS** |

Representative failing canonical request (test B):

```
GET
/workflow%3Dmy_workflow_id/schedule%3Dadhoc/2026-07-23T19%3A30%3A45.513Z-my_workflow_id.csv

host:my-bucket.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
x-amz-content-sha256:e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
x-amz-date:20260723T193148Z

host;x-amz-content-sha256;x-amz-date
e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
```

**Two conclusions from this table:**

1. **The `accept` header is not the cause.** B and C did *not* sign `accept` and failed identically to E, which did. The only invariant across every failure is the percent-encoded path.
2. **Test F is the smoking gun.** Supplying the key *already* percent-encoded makes signed == sent, and the request succeeds — confirming the signature is computed over the un-encoded form while the encoded form is transmitted.

## Secondary bug — region parsed from hostname (test D)

Using the HTTP Request node with an AWS predefined credential against a **virtual-hosted-style** S3 URL:

```
https://my-bucket.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/<key>
```

fails with:

```
Unsupported AWS region "s3" parsed from endpoint host my-bucket.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
```

The host is split on `.` and segment `[1]` is taken as the region — which is `"s3"` for virtual-hosted-style URLs. Only path-style (`s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/<bucket>/…`) parses correctly. Virtual-hosted-style is the AWS-recommended default, so this should be supported.

## Workaround

Percent-encode the key per path segment and fetch via HTTP Request + AWS credential over a **path-style** URL:

```js
const encodedKey = key.split('/').map(encodeURIComponent).join('/');
const downloadUrl = `https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/${bucket}/${encodedKey}`;
```

This is fragile by nature: **if the signer is fixed, this workaround will double-encode and break.** A proper fix in n8n is needed.

## Environment

- **n8n version:** 2.31.5 (Cloud) — regression from 2.29.8, where this worked
- **Database:** n8n Cloud default
- **Running n8n via:** n8n Cloud
- **Operating system:** n/a (managed)
- **Affected nodes:** `n8n-nodes-base.awsS3` (typeVersion 1 and 2), `n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest` (4.2) with `nodeCredentialType: aws`
- **Stack (V2):** `n8n-nodes-base/nodes/Aws/S3/V2/GenericFunctions.ts:45` → `n8n-core/.../request-helpers/authentication.ts:263`

## Impact

Breaks every S3 read against Hive-partitioned prefixes — Amazon Marketing Cloud result delivery, Athena/Glue query output, Spark/EMR output. In our case it silently took down two production data pipelines; the only visible symptom was a 403 that reads like a credentials problem, which sends you chasing the wrong cause.

title: Wait node ("On Form Submitted") resumeUrl returns 404 in production, but works fine in manual/test execution — path changes from /form-waiting/ to /webhook-waiting/
thread_text: TITLE: Wait node ("On Form Submitted") resumeUrl returns 404 in production, but works fine in manual/test execution — path changes from /form-waiting/ to /webhook-waiting/ ISSUE DESCRIPTION: ### Bug Description When using a Wait node configured to resume "On Form Submitted", and sending {{ $execution.resumeUrl }} to the user (via a Telegram message in my case), the resume link works correctly when testing the workflow manually (not activated). However, once the workflow is activated/published, following the exact same type of link and submitting the form fails with a 404 error. Comparing the two cases in DevTools Network tab shows the generated resumeUrl uses a *different path prefix* depending on execution mode, even though the Wait node's "Resume On" setting is unchanged (Form Submitted): - Manual/test execution: `POST /form-waiting/{executionId}?signature=...` → 200 OK - Activated/production execution: `POST /webhook-waiting/{executionId}?signature=...` → 404 Not Found This suggests that when the workflow is active, the Wait node's Form-resume generates the wrong endpoint type (webhook-waiting instead of form-waiting). I was able to reproduce this both on my self-hosted instance (Docker, Queue mode, PostgreSQL, behind Cloudflare) and on n8n Cloud, so this does not appear to be environment or reverse-proxy specific. ### To Reproduce 1. Create a workflow: Telegram Trigger → "Send a text message" node containing {{ $execution.resumeUrl }} → Wait node (Resume: "On Form Submitted") 2. Trigger the workflow manually / without activating it → open the Telegram message → follow the resume link → submit the form → works fine (200, path is /form-waiting/...) 3. Activate/publish the workflow 4. Trigger it again via Telegram → open the new resume link → submit the form → fails with 404 (path is /webhook-waiting/...) ### Expected behavior The resume link generated by a Wait node set to "On Form Submitted" should behave consistently and use the /form-waiting/ endpoint regardless of whether the workflow is running in manual/test mode or in activated/production mode. ### Debug Info # Debug info ## core - n8nVersion: 2.30.7 - platform: docker (self-hosted) - nodeJsVersion: 24.16.0 - nodeEnv: production - database: postgres - executionMode: scaling (single-main) - concurrency: -1 - license: enterprise (production) - consumerId: 492a89d9-75cd-46e7-939f-8ff42e73a166 ## storage - success: all - error: all - progress: false - manual: true - binaryMode: database ## pruning - enabled: true - maxAge: 336 hours - maxCount: 10000 executions ## client - userAgent: mozilla/5.0 (x11; ubuntu; linux x86_64; rv:152.0) gecko/20100101 firefox/152.0 - isTouchDevice: false ## cluster - instanceCount: 2 - versions: 2.30.7 - instances: - instanceKey: b65e31ba-b07f-4ebe-a2e5-b77b5ecea590, hostId: worker-1baca08a4594, instanceType: worker, instanceRole: unset, version: 2.30.7 - instanceKey: 6f490f3a-216e-4ef7-995c-ea5962bc2b62, hostId: main-4cdd101a21c3, instanceType: main, instanceRole: leader, version: 2.30.7 - checks: - check: hostid-clash, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: lifecycle, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: split-brain, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: version-mismatch, status: succeeded, warnings: - Generated at: 2026-07-19T14:42:10.591Z ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04.4 ### n8n Version 2.30.7 ### Node.js Version 24.16.0 ### Database PostgreSQL ### Execution mode queue ### Hosting self hosted
